reviews.review: i´ve never played a better optimize unreal engine game than back 4 blood : good job

Such a bad game and big disappointment, PvP mode is broken, as people keep leaving, because they want to play as zombies and not survivors and they dont get a penalty for doing so. 

Also in campaign the difficulty is either way too hard or way too easy. Furthermore you cant find players to play with.

TL;DR: Loved it, and then mandatory full deck draw ruined it for me. Now it's just another zombie FPS.

So, I need to vent, even if I'm just shouting into a wind tunnel. This was one of my favorite games, by far. Was. A fascinating and unique thing that I played obsessively for quite a while. I felt no real need to compare it to the L4D games that much, and none of the complaints I ever groused about were dealbreakers. I felt like the balance changes the devs were making generally seemed helpful or at least reasonable, and generally considered this to be probably one of my ultrafavs, my shortlist.

I can't play the same thing all the time forever, though, of course, so I drifted into other things, knowing I'd probably come back at some point. 

Noticing about updates and just plain wondering how the game was developing, I started it up and jumped in and started playing. It actually took me a bit to realize why it just felt wrong. So, let's talk about the stupid full deck draw. Some cursory research makes it appear that is still the only option, and if that's no longer correct, I'll happily change basically all of this.

The card system was the unique and interesting mechanism for me. There are tactical elements to setting up your deck in advance, having to consider the order you unlock them versus your progression through the campaign, but there's also a degree of flexibility "in the field", since you got to pick from among the next few cards, letting you respond to the abilities and styles of your teammates, the corruption cards, and so on. Do I want to use this card that disables ADS this time around, when I have a teammate focusing on close combat already? Maybe not, so I'll skip it this time. That sort of thing.

Replayability, variability, experimenting with card combinations, etc, in a fun and different way than other games went about it.

In addition to those practical elements, I don't think I was even aware of it until it was bloody taken away, but it gave a fantastic sense of actual progression. Starting off struggling and having to barely make do, and then getting stronger as the campaign did was, in retrospect, the spice of it all. Not just in terms of us the actual players, or getting bigger, badder guns, but getting faster, sturdier, and even entire new abilities. The *characters* got to evolve over the course of the game, not just the enemies, players, or equipment. It also introduced this excellent boardgame-feeling element, knowing you have only a limited number of "turns" to accomplish all that you want to, sort of. 

I'm almost certain I've never played anything quite like it, and not noticing they'd changed this but noticing they'd done other stuff, I was very eager to jump in and discover all that was new, and after playing a bit, was feeling a bit miffed. I went to play solo for a bit to try and figure out what was wrong, and pretty much right away then realized it was giving me all the cards. Obnoxious. Went and dug around in the menus, wondering what new thing they'd turned on. Found nothing. Turned to the internet, and saw a lot of things that used language like "*allows* players to draw the full deck," "*adds* full deck draw," "full deck draw now *possible*," etc, heavily implicating that it's optional, but more digging found what seemed like not very many people having the same complaint as I - that you can't turn it off.

The field flexibility is now gone. The characters are basically as they are from start to end. You get to stomp all over the beginning of the game like some kind of demigod, only to feel progressively crappier as the enemies step up their game and you don't. It's just like a hundred other games, where you screw around in the menus and pick out your equipment, abilities, whatever the game uses, probably find the one that works best for you, and then *never* care about the cards again.

I just seriously can't wrap my head around it. I feel that this is otherwise a pretty fantastically well polished and realized game, and I was so pleased that this team pulled that off. But without this unique spice, it's still... kind of just a first person zombie shooter. Campaign, multiplayer PVE, two guns, gun mods, various grenades, situational tools, melee/bash, zombies, headshots, bigger and scarier zombies, weakpoints, urban environments, health management. I'm sitting here trying to dig through my memory to find anything of note, but just... NONE of this is anything that special. This one is quite well constructed, and if I hadn't been given that unique experience before, that might've been enough to keep me periodically coming back and binging the heck out of it every so often. But I did get to have that, and now it's just ruined for me.

I don't care if this was how the highest difficulty did it before, that might be fair enough, though I feel like adjusting the draw rate should probably work. I can't care about any of the new bits and bobs or possibly fun stuff. It's all, presently, just pointless. To me, it's compounded by the high expectations I have, or at least had, for Turtle Rock, and the fact that it doesn't seem like all that many people care. I let it rest for a couple of months to see if it changed, or what the community reaction might be, but it doesn't seem to have really changed, and I just can't care enough to give the rest of it a shake now.

All in all, this is legitimately so aggravating, disappointing, and pretty much heartbreaking that, even knowing it to be almost certainly in vain, I was still compelled to use my Saturday afternoon to write my longest to date - and first ever negative - review.

Thanks for the short-lived interesting experience, I guess. For a brief time, I had *so much* fun, but unless this changes, and soon enough for me to still care and people to still be playing it, this is now on my shortlist of most disappointing things ever.
I love playing this game with my friends, super fun, lots of different challenging aspects, lots of different difficulties for new and experienced players. Would highly recommend!
